question.text: The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown above. Which of the following is the graph of $y=f\left(\dfrac{1}{4}x\right)?$
question.explanation:
To graph the function $y = f\left(\dfrac{1}{4}x\right),$ we take the graph of $y = f(x)$ and stretch it by factor of $4$ parallel to the $x$-axis. This has the effect of multiplying the $x$-coordinates of all points on $y=f(x)$ by $4.$

The resulting graph is shown below.

question.text: The point $P$ with coordinates $(-6, 9)$ lies on the curve $y =f(x).$ Which of the following points must lie on $y = f\left(\dfrac{1}{3}x\right)?$
question.explanation:
The function $y = f\left(\dfrac{1}{3}x\right)$ represents a stretch of the function $y = f(x)$ by a factor of $3$ parallel to the $x$-axis. This has the effect of multiplying the $x$-coordinates of all points on $y=f(x)$ by $3.$

Therefore, the point $(-6,9)$ on $f(x)$ is mapped to the point $\left(3\cdot (-6) , 9\right) = (-18,9),$ and this point must lie on the graph of $y = f\left(\dfrac{1}{3}x\right)$

example.title: Finding a Point that Lies on a Horizontally Stretched Function
